title: The OPTIC-K voicing cloud, from 1,000 to 1,000,000 points: Points, instancing, WebGPU compute
question: GA's OPTIC-K index holds 313k voicings as 112-dimensional vectors. Projected to 3D, how many can a browser draw as Points, as instanced octahedra, and animate (a morph between two projections) on the CPU or in a WebGPU compute shader?
hypothesis: 1-pixel Points stay cheap up to 1M; instanced octahedra cost 8 triangles each and fall behind; animating 1M points on the CPU is limited by the loop and the 12 MB upload per frame, which a compute shader removes.

predictions.metric: median GPU ms per frame, Points, 1M points
median GPU ms per frame, instanced octahedra, 1M
median CPU ms per frame, morph on the CPU, 1M
median CPU ms per frame, morph in a compute shader, 1M

predictions.predicted: compute does not run on the WebGL 2 backend; the page reports it
